name: Achalasia

criteria.description: Absent normal peristalsis (100% failed or spastic contractions)
Type I: absent contractility (no esophageal pressurization)
Type II: panesophageal pressurization in >= 20% of swallows
Type III: premature (spastic) contractions in >= 20% of swallows
Timed barium esophagram showing esophageal dilation with bird-beak narrowing at GEJ

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated IRP and absent normal peristalsis on high-resolution manometry. Pseudoachalasia (malignancy) must be excluded.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Chicago Classification v4.0 further subdivides into Types I, II, III based on contractile pattern. Type II has best treatment response.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dysphagia to both solids and liquids
pathognomonic.notes: Simultaneous onset for both solids and liquids is characteristic
Bland, non-acidic regurgitation of retained food/saliva

common.notes: More common in Type III (spastic) achalasia
From stasis rather than true acid reflux
Due to aspiration of retained esophageal contents

rare.notes: Long-standing untreated achalasia carries increased cancer risk
Rare complication of massive esophageal dilation

laboratory: Anti-myenteric neuronal antibodies may be present (research use)
imaging: Timed barium esophagram: dilated esophagus with bird-beak tapering at GEJ
Chest X-ray may show absent gastric air bubble, widened mediastinum, air-fluid level
CT chest may show dilated esophagus with retained food/fluid
genetic: Rare familial cases linked to Allgrove syndrome (AAAS gene, triple-A syndrome)
other: High-resolution manometry is the gold standard diagnostic test
Upper endoscopy: dilated esophagus with retained food, puckered GEJ, resistance at cardia
Endoscopic ultrasound to exclude pseudoachalasia from submucosal tumors

distinguishingFeatures: EoE typically causes dysphagia to solids primarily
EoE shows eosinophilic infiltrate on biopsy
EoE has normal LES relaxation on manometry
Pseudoachalasia from GEJ tumor: older age, rapid onset, marked weight loss
CT/EUS shows mass at GEJ in pseudoachalasia
Chagas disease is endemic to Central/South America
Positive Trypanosoma cruzi serology in Chagas

redFlags: Rapid onset of dysphagia (< 6 months) in patient > 55 years (rule out pseudoachalasia from malignancy)
Marked weight loss disproportionate to dysphagia severity
references: Yadlapati R, et al. Esophageal motility disorders on high-resolution manometry: Chicago Classification version 4.0. Neurogastroenterol Motil. 2021;33(1):e14058.
Vaezi MF, et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Achalasia. Am J Gastroenterol. 2020;115(9):1393-1411.
Oude Nijhuis RAB, et al. European Guideline on Achalasia: UEG and ESNM recommendations. United European Gastroenterol J. 2020;8(1):13-33.
